To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a QTL for hyperglycemic in KK mice was identified on chromosome 6, and that the Ay allele may interact with QTLs accounting for glucose tolerance.

the genetic loci for hyperglycemic traits in KK mice may be masked by strong hyperglycemia of the Ay allele, and that the genetic locis accounting for impaired glucose tolerance interact with the Ay locus, since they were identified only in the F2 Ay/a mice.

1) a QTL on chromosome 6 was responsible for fasting glucose levels in KK mice, 2) the Ay allele was responsible for impaired glucose tolerance in these mice, and 3) the Ay allele interacted with QTLs on chromosomes 1, 8, and 9 to enhance the glucose intolerance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of QTLs in mice with impaired glucose tolerance and hyperglycemia, which may be relevant to non insulin dependent diabetes in humans.
the analysis of the genetic basis of diabetes in mice.
the genetic dissection of hyperglycemia, impaired glucose tolerance and insulin resistance in KK mice, and the identification of genes responsible for these phenotypes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the KK mouse may be a useful model for human NIDDM in that it has a number of QTLs which control fasting glucose levels.

the KK mouse is not suitable as a polygenetic model for human noninsulin-dependent diabetes mellitus, since it does not have all of the features of the human disease, and that the KK Ay mouse may be a better model.
the QTL for the hyperglycemic trait in KK mice is on chromosome 6, and that the impaired glucose intolerance is controlled by Q TLs on chromosomes 1, 8 and 9.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the KK mouse is suitable for the identification of genes involved in hyperglycemia in the presence of the Ay allele, but not for the identification of those involved in impaired glucose tolerance in the absence of the Ay allele
there are at least 5 loci on 5 different chromosomes that contribute to hyperglycemia in KK mice, but the major QTL for fasting hyperglycemia is on chromosome 6.
the agouti gene on chromosome 2 is a major gene for fasting glucose levels in KK mice, while the Ay allele on chromosome 9 is a major gene responsible for impaired glucose tolerance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single QTL on chromosome 6 accounts for fasting hyperglycemia in KK mice and is not affected by the Ay allele.
the genetic analysis of KK mice should take into account the genetic background of the Ay allele.
the Ay allele has a strong influence on glucose tolerance in KK Ay mice.
